source.title: NORAD/CONAD Historical Summary, July-December 1963
source.holder: The Black Vault declassified-scan mirror; official NORAD history inventory lists the title
source.read_method: Scanned pages visually inspected, PDF indexes 70/71; hash is of the exact mirrored binary downloaded 2026-11-14

events.finding: JCS advised NORAD that the three SAO-operated cameras would not be available under the proposed transfer; requested plan for four USAF-owned cameras plus Cold Lake.
JCS requested every effort to have NASA provide Baker-Nunn data to SPADATS; this documents a request, not receipt of any named measurement.
NORAD described a revised mutually supporting USAF/RCAF camera subsystem, with SAO camera contributions still to be determined before recommendations.
NORAD learned that the Navy no longer required Baker-Nunn cameras for SPASUR calibration and JCS approved no further action on this calibration request.
The report states secure communication circuits scheduled for 15 November at Cold Lake had still not been installed by the end of 1963; operational control did not prove direct real-time data feed.

next_test: Recover actual 1963 tracking log with NORAD 528/1963-003B, station, UTC timestamp, observable, reference frame, calibration and error; audit actual NSA/NASA/SAO-to-SPADATS data transfers.
